Source: none. This notebook audits the join of the interim outputs of
scripts 01-03 into the municipality-year panel of the Amazon-biome sample
(503 municipalities, 2000-2020) and the three derived blocks added at the
join (pooled z-scores of the price indices, per-capita Bolsa Família
transfers; the electoral lag retired at step 2.3; the two municipality
flags of step 2.5).
Pipeline script: `_scripts/04-panel-assemble.R`.
Interim output: `_data/interim/panel_amz_2000_2020.rds`.
Equivalence with the recovered panel is not checked here (the notebook never
reads `_data/reference/`); the `compare_outputs` report lives in the phase 1
script 04 commit message and in the decision entries it cites.

```{r setup}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
})
options(width = 110)
```

```{r read}
panel <- read_rds("_data/interim/panel_amz_2000_2020.rds")
mapbiomas <- read_rds("_data/interim/mapbiomas_deforestation_amz_1987_2023.rds")
ppcdam <- read_rds("_data/interim/ppcdam_list_2004_2024.rds")
munic_area <- read_rds("_data/interim/pam_ppm_munic_area_2022.rds")
sample_geocodes <- unique(mapbiomas$geocode)
```

## Q1. Which sources cover which municipality-years of the 503 × 21 panel?

What is checked: for one representative column per source block, the
number of non-missing cells by year. A left join from the MapBiomas sample
leaves NA wherever a source has no row, and the sources have different
windows (Bolsa Família 2004-2019, GDP and population 2002 onward, prices
2000-2020 with the crop lag from 2001).

```{r q1-coverage}
blocks <- c(mapbiomas = "forest_area_km2", ppcdam = "ppcdam_list",
            bf = "bf_families_n", rais = "emp_pia_rate_total",
            census = "informal", ibge_pib = "population",
            tse = "elec_enc", area = "munic_area_km2",
            pam = "crop_soy_area_planted_km2", ppm = "cattle_heads",
            prices = "price_index_crop")
panel %>%
  select(year, all_of(unname(blocks))) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(!is.na(.x))), .groups = "drop") %>%
  rename(!!!set_names(unname(blocks), names(blocks))) %>%
  print(n = 21)
```

```{r q1-municipalities}
panel %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(unname(blocks)),
                   ~ n_distinct(geocode[!is.na(.x)]))) %>%
  rename(!!!set_names(unname(blocks), names(blocks))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "block",
               values_to = "municipalities_with_data")
```

```{r q1-na-cells}
panel %>%
  select(geocode, all_of(unname(blocks))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-geocode, names_to = "column") %>%
  filter(is.na(value)) %>%
  group_by(column) %>%
  summarise(na_cells = n(), municipalities = n_distinct(geocode),
            .groups = "drop")
```

**Finding.** All 503 municipalities have rows in every block except RAIS
(Mojuí dos Campos has none) and the PAM crop block with the crop index
(Santa Cruz do Arari has no series, D-2026-10-10-i). Within the sources'
windows the gaps are: Bolsa Família 2004-2019 only; population and GDP
from 2002, with the nine Mato Grosso municipalities absent from the 2000
census NA through 2009 (72 cells, D-2026-10-05-k); RAIS 72
municipality-years (Mojuí's 21 and 51 early years of small municipalities,
`_audit/rais.qmd` Q2, task 1.8); elections 28 cells (Mojuí 2000-2011 and
four municipalities installed in 2001 for 2000-2003); cattle 30 cells and
crop areas 112 cells (Mojuí before 2013, the post-2000 Mato Grosso
municipalities before their first survey year, D-2026-10-10-g, Santa Cruz
do Arari, and scattered years of six Pará municipalities of the Belém
metropolitan area and the Marajó). Everything else is complete over
2000-2020.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-11-a (left joins onto the MapBiomas sample, 503
municipalities including Mojuí dos Campos); D-2026-10-11-g (columns not
carried into the panel).
**Assertion.** `04-panel-assemble.R`, raw-state block (unique keys, 503
geocodes, every sample municipality in the areas file) and output block
(503 × 21 rows, unique keys).

## Q2. Which PPCDAm municipalities fall outside the biome sample, and how is the indicator coded where the list is silent?

What is checked: the listed municipalities absent from the 503, and the
count of listed municipality-years by year after NA is recoded to 0.

```{r q2-outside}
ppcdam %>%
  filter(!geocode %in% sample_geocodes) %>%
  group_by(geocode, municipality) %>%
  summarise(listed_years = paste(year[ppcdam_list == 1L], collapse = ", "),
            .groups = "drop")
```

```{r q2-listed}
panel %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(listed = sum(ppcdam_list), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = listed)
```

**Finding.** Four listed municipalities are not in the IBGE Amazônia
predominant-biome list and leave the panel at the join: Grajaú (MA,
listed from 2011) and three Mato Grosso municipalities listed only in
2023-2024 (Comodoro, Paranatinga, Ribeirão Cascalheira). Grajaú is the one
ever-listed municipality that the Legal Amazon extension (task 1.1) adds
within the 2004-2020 window. The list file carries 0 for 2004-2007 and the
join leaves NA for 2000-2003 and for every never-listed municipality; both
are recoded to 0, so the indicator is never NA and is 0 before 2008.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-11-b.
**Assertion.** `04-panel-assemble.R`, raw-state block (four outside
geocodes, values in {0, 1}) and output block (no NA, zero before 2008).

## Q3. Are the areas on one unit?

What is checked: the MapBiomas forest area (in km² from script 01 since
phase 2, step 2.8, D-2026-10-28-j; converted at the join before) as a
share of the IBGE municipal area (the 2025 release at phase 1; the 2022
release from phase 2, step 2.7, D-2026-10-28-g); any share above 1 is a
unit or boundary problem. The second chunk compares the total area
MapBiomas Collection 9 maps for each municipality (all transition classes
summed, constant across years) with the IBGE area in the panel, to
separate the two; the third shows the 2025 release for the three
municipalities of the Boa Esperança do Norte split.

```{r q3-share}
share <- panel %>%
  transmute(geocode, municipality, state_abbreviation, year,
            forest_share = forest_area_km2 / munic_area_km2,
            total_share = (forest_area_km2 + deforestation_area_km2) /
              munic_area_km2)
summary(share$forest_share)
share %>% filter(forest_share > 1)
```

```{r q3-mesh}
mapbiomas_raw <- readxl::read_xlsx("_data/raw/mapbiomas/mapbiomas_munic.xlsx",
                                   sheet = "DEF_SECVEG")
mapped_total <- mapbiomas_raw %>%
  mutate(geocode = as.character(geocode)) %>%
  filter(geocode %in% sample_geocodes) %>%
  group_by(geocode) %>%
  summarise(mapped_total_km2_2000 = sum(`2000`) / 100,
            mapped_total_km2_2023 = sum(`2023`) / 100, .groups = "drop")
mesh <- mapped_total %>%
  left_join(munic_area, by = "geocode") %>%
  left_join(distinct(mapbiomas, geocode, municipality, state_abbreviation),
            by = "geocode") %>%
  mutate(ratio = mapped_total_km2_2023 / munic_area_km2)
c(max_year_change_km2 = max(abs(mesh$mapped_total_km2_2000 -
                                  mesh$mapped_total_km2_2023)),
  n_within_1pct = sum(abs(mesh$ratio - 1) <= 0.01),
  n_over_2pct = sum(abs(mesh$ratio - 1) > 0.02))
mesh %>%
  filter(abs(ratio - 1) > 0.02) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(ratio - 1))) %>%
  transmute(geocode, municipality, state_abbreviation,
            mapped_total_km2 = round(mapped_total_km2_2023, 1),
            munic_area_km2 = round(munic_area_km2, 1),
            ratio = round(ratio, 3))
readxl::read_excel("_data/raw/ibge/AR_BR_RG_UF_RGINT_RGI_MUN_2025.xls",
                   sheet = "AR_BR_MUN_2025", col_types = "text") %>%
  filter(CD_MUN %in% c("5101837", "5106240", "5107925")) %>%
  transmute(geocode = CD_MUN, municipality = NM_MUN,
            munic_area_km2_2025 = round(as.numeric(AR_MUN_2025), 1),
            in_mapbiomas = geocode %in% as.character(mapbiomas_raw$geocode))
```

**Finding.** With the 2022 release (phase 2, step 2.7, 2026-10-28) the
forest share of the municipal area lies between 0.06 and 1.0 in every
municipality-year, and the mapped total agrees with the area within 1
percent for 486 of the 503 municipalities; the 7 that differ by more than
2 percent are coastal municipalities of Maranhão and Pará where MapBiomas
maps less than the area in either release (pam_ppm.qmd Q7). At phase 1,
with the 2025 release, four municipality-years broke the bound: Nova
Ubiratã (MT) in 2000-2003, where the converted forest area exceeded the
municipal area by up to 18 percent. That was a mesh-vintage mismatch, not
a unit error: MapBiomas Collection 9 maps 12,461 km² for Nova Ubiratã in
every year, against 8,721 km² in the 2025 IBGE table, because Boa
Esperança do Norte (MT, geocode 5101837, 4,704 km², installed 2025) was
carved out of Nova Ubiratã (3,740 km²) and Sorriso (839 km², Cerrado,
outside the sample), with small parts of Vera and Paranatinga; the new
municipality is in the 2025 table and absent from MapBiomas, from the
biome list and from the 2022 table. Every 2000-2020 variable of Nova
Ubiratã refers to the pre-split territory, so with the post-split area its
cattle density and crop shares were inflated by 43 percent in every year;
the 2025 area agreed with the mapped total within 1 percent for 459
municipalities and differed by more than 2 percent in 20, the largest
after Nova Ubiratã being the Seringueiras-São Miguel do Guaporé (RO)
boundary swap of 670 km² (0.85 and 1.10). The fall of Nova Ubiratã's
forest plus deforestation from 10,480 km² in 2000 to 8,935 km² in 2004 is
class composition (D-2026-10-06-b): land cleared in year t is "Antrópico"
from t+1, so it leaves both classes.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-28-j (phase 2, step 2.8: hectares to km² at
construction in script 01, the interim columns under their panel names;
supersedes D-2026-10-11-c, the conversion at the join); D-2026-10-28-g (the 2022 release, the mesh of Collection 9,
superseding the vintage of D-2026-10-10-f).
**Assertion.** `04-panel-assemble.R`, output block
(`N_FOREST_OVER_AREA_EXPECTED` = 0).

## Q4. Do the pooled z-scores have mean 0 and sd 1, and how much does Santa Cruz do Arari's restored cattle index move them?

What is checked: the moments of the four z-scores, and the cattle z-score
recomputed with the municipality's 21 restored cells (D-2026-10-10-i) left
out of the pool.

```{r q4-moments}
panel %>%
  summarise(across(ends_with("_z"),
                   list(mean = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                        sd = ~ sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                        na = ~ sum(is.na(.x))))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("variable", "stat"),
               names_pattern = "(.*)_(mean|sd|na)$") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = stat, values_from = value)
```

```{r q4-santa-cruz}
x <- panel$price_index_cattle
pool_without <- if_else(panel$geocode == "1506401", NA_real_, x)
z_with <- (x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
z_without <- (x - mean(pool_without, na.rm = TRUE)) /
  sd(pool_without, na.rm = TRUE)
tibble(max_abs_shift = max(abs(z_with - z_without), na.rm = TRUE),
       cells_shifted = sum(abs(z_with - z_without) > 1e-8, na.rm = TRUE))
```

**Finding.** Every z-score has mean 0 and sd 1 to numerical precision;
the crop z-score is NA where the crop index is NA (Santa Cruz do Arari
and, since D-2026-10-23-b, Ipiranga do Norte, Itanhangá and Mojuí dos
Campos, whose zeros left the pool) and the lags are NA in 2000. Adding Santa Cruz do Arari's restored index
to the pool shifts the cattle z-score of every cell by at most about four
thousandths of a standard deviation; the rest of the drift reported by the
comparator for the z-scores is the Pink Sheet release (D-2026-10-10-a)
passed through the standardisation.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-11-d; the pooled standardisation is
sample-dependent and is flagged for the storage audit (task 2.2).
**Assertion.** `04-panel-assemble.R`, output block (moments within
`Z_TOL`, cattle lag NA in 2000).

## Q5. Are the electoral columns stored on the governing years?

What is checked: one municipality's effective number of candidates and
winner's party across the 2004 and 2008 elections; NA counts of the
electoral block by year. Until phase 2, step 2.3 (2026-10-22) the stored
block changed in the election year and script 04 added a one-year lag with
the `_gov` suffix (D-2026-10-11-e); since the step, script 03 stores the
values on the governing years and the lag is retired (D-2026-10-22-d, -e;
`_audit/tse.qmd` Q4, Q7).

```{r q5-alignment}
panel %>%
  filter(geocode == "1100015", year %in% 2003:2010) %>%
  select(year, election_year, elec_enc, elec_winner_party, elec_mov, elec_competitive)
```

```{r q5-na}
panel %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(na_enc = sum(is.na(elec_enc)), na_mov = sum(is.na(elec_mov)),
            uncontested = sum(elec_uncontested, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(na_enc > 0 | na_mov > 0)
panel %>%
  filter(year > 2000, is.na(elec_enc)) %>%
  group_by(geocode, municipality) %>%
  summarise(years = paste(range(year), collapse = "-"), .groups = "drop")
```

**Finding.** The stored block changes the year after each election (2005,
2009): the governing-period rule. In 2000 every electoral column is NA
because the 1996 election is outside the data; after 2000 the margin and
the competitive flag are NA exactly on the uncontested races, and the 28
municipality-years with no value at all are those without a governing
election in the file (Mojuí dos Campos 2001-2012; Ipiranga do Norte,
Itanhangá, Altamira do Maranhão and Brejo de Areia 2001-2004).
**Decision.** D-2026-10-22-d (storage), D-2026-10-22-e (`_gov` retired;
supersedes D-2026-10-11-e).
**Assertion.** `04-panel-assemble.R`, output block (2000 NA; 28 NA
municipality-years after 2000; margin and flag NA iff uncontested or no
election).

## Q6. Where are per-capita transfers missing, and why?

What is checked: non-missing cells of `bf_transfers_pc_brl_2024` by year
against the transfers and the population it divides.

```{r q6-coverage}
panel %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(transfers = sum(!is.na(bf_transfers_total_brl_2024)),
            population = sum(!is.na(population)),
            per_capita = sum(!is.na(bf_transfers_pc_brl_2024)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(transfers > 0)
```

**Finding.** Per-capita transfers exist exactly where both inputs do.
Since phase 2, step 2.5 (2026-10-23) population is complete from each
municipality's installation (D-2026-10-23-e), so the per-capita column is
missing only where the transfers are; until then the nine Mato Grosso
municipalities without a 2000 census population were NA through 2009
(D-2026-10-05-k). No municipality-year has a zero population.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-11-f; D-2026-10-23-e (closes D-2026-10-10-k).
**Assertion.** `04-panel-assemble.R`, output block (NA pattern equals the
union of the inputs' NA).

## Q7. What does the panel hold for Mojuí dos Campos?

What is checked: the non-missing years of each block for geocode 1504752,
kept in this panel and dropped in script 05 (D-2026-10-05-l), as evidence
for the author's review of that drop (GitHub issue #8).

```{r q7-mojui}
panel %>%
  filter(geocode == "1504752") %>%
  select(year, all_of(unname(blocks)), bf_transfers_pc_brl_2024) %>%
  rename(!!!set_names(unname(blocks), names(blocks))) %>%
  summarise(across(-year, ~ if (any(!is.na(.x))) {
    paste(range(year[!is.na(.x)]), collapse = "-")
  } else {
    "none"
  })) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "block", values_to = "years_with_data")
```

**Finding.** Mojuí dos Campos carries deforestation, area and PPCDAm
(never listed) for every year; since phase 2, step 2.5 (2026-10-23) its
GDP and population start in 2013 (official estimates to 2021, the 2022
census) and the census block in 2022, the split with Santarém being
retired (D-2026-10-23-f); PAM and PPM series from 2013; elections from
the 2012 election; Bolsa Família from 2014. The crop index is NA (all
base-window weights missing, D-2026-10-23-b) and so is the cattle index.
It has no RAIS row at all. The RAIS gap and the series before 2013 are
what re-inclusion would have to solve.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-05-l (provisional; issue #8); D-2026-10-23-f.
**Assertion.** none; the row count assertion counts it among the 503.

## Q8. Which municipalities carry the post-2000 and parent flags?

What is checked: the lookup rows against the sample municipalities with no
2000 population, the parents named in the lookup against the flag, and the
time-invariance of both flags (phase 2, step 2.5).

```{r q8-flags}
post2000 <- read_csv("_data/aux/munic_post2000.csv",
                     col_types = cols(.default = col_character(), install_year = col_integer()))
post2000 %>% select(geocode, municipality, install_year, parent_names)
panel %>%
  filter(year == 2000, is.na(population)) %>%
  select(geocode, municipality, muni_new_post2000)
panel %>%
  filter(year == 2000, muni_parent_split == 1L) %>%
  select(geocode, municipality, state_abbreviation)
setdiff(unique(unlist(str_split(post2000$parent_geocodes, ";"))), sample_geocodes)
panel %>%
  group_by(geocode) %>%
  summarise(across(c(muni_new_post2000, muni_parent_split), n_distinct), .groups = "drop") %>%
  summarise(across(-geocode, max))
```

**Finding.** Ten municipalities carry `muni_new_post2000`: the nine Mato
Grosso municipalities installed in 2001 and 2005 and Mojuí dos Campos
(2013), exactly the set with no population in 2000. Ten of their twelve
parents are in the biome sample and carry `muni_parent_split`; Ribeirão
Cascalheira and Cáceres are outside it. Both flags are constant within
municipality. Installation years, parents and laws stay in the lookup.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-23-f.
**Assertion.** `04-panel-assemble.R`, output block (the NA-population set
in 2000 equals the lookup; ten flagged in each column).

## Q9. Do the denominator counts and the installation rule hold in the panel? (phase 2, step 2.7, 2026-10-28)

What is checked: the three counts carried from script 02
(`emp_workers_n`, `emp_agri_workers_n`, `pia`), the NA set they share
with the `emp_*` rates and shares, the 0 / 0 pattern of the agricultural
shares, and the first observed year of each source against the
installation year of the lookup (task 1.8; D-2026-10-28-a, -b, -d).

```{r q9-counts}
post2000 <- read_csv("_data/aux/munic_post2000.csv",
                     col_types = cols(.default = col_character(), install_year = col_integer()))
panel %>%
  summarise(across(c(emp_workers_n, emp_agri_workers_n, pia),
                   list(na = ~ sum(is.na(.x)), zero = ~ sum(.x == 0, na.rm = TRUE))))
emp_absent <- panel %>%
  filter(is.na(emp_workers_n)) %>%
  left_join(post2000 %>% select(geocode, install_year), by = "geocode") %>%
  mutate(kind = if_else(!is.na(install_year) & year < install_year, "before installation", "gap"))
emp_absent %>% count(kind)
panel %>%
  mutate(agri = case_when(is.na(emp_agri_workers_n) ~ "absent", emp_agri_workers_n == 0 ~ "zero",
                          TRUE ~ "positive")) %>%
  group_by(agri) %>%
  summarise(cells = n(), across(c(emp_share_agri_low_workers, emp_share_agri_high_workers),
                                ~ sum(is.na(.x)), .names = "na_{.col}"), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r q9-install}
first_obs <- function(x, year) if (all(is.na(x))) NA_integer_ else min(year[!is.na(x)])
panel %>%
  inner_join(post2000 %>% select(geocode, install_year), by = "geocode") %>%
  group_by(municipality, install_year) %>%
  summarise(crops = first_obs(crop_soy_area_planted_km2, year), cattle = first_obs(cattle_heads, year),
            employment = first_obs(emp_workers_n, year), population = first_obs(population, year),
            gdp = first_obs(gdp_brl, year), bf = first_obs(bf_families_n, year),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(install_year, municipality)
```

**Finding.** `emp_workers_n` and `emp_agri_workers_n` are NA in the 64
municipality-years absent from the RAIS export, 30 before installation
and 34 reporting gaps, the same cells where every `emp_*` rate and share
is NA; `pia`, joined from the census file and not from the RAIS rows, is
NA where `pea` is: before 2010 for the nine municipalities without a
2000 anchor and in every year for Mojuí dos Campos (111 cells). The agricultural shares are NA in
the absent cells and where `emp_agri_workers_n` is 0, nowhere else. For
the ten lookup municipalities every source starts in the installation
year (GDP from 2002 for those installed in 2001; Bolsa Família from 2014
for Mojuí dos Campos, whose code enters the MDS files a year late) and is
NA before it.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-28-a, D-2026-10-28-b, D-2026-10-28-d.
**Assertion.** `04-panel-assemble.R`, output block (64 NA cells shared
by the counts, rates and shares; 111 NA cells of `pia`, the NA set of
`pea`; agricultural shares NA iff absent or zero agricultural bonds;
`INSTALL_RULE_COLS` NA before the installation year and observed from
it).

## Q10. Is every share and rate on 0-1, and does each column's range fit its codebook unit? (phase 2, step 2.8, 2026-10-28)

What is checked: the range of every numeric column of the final panel
against the `unit` the codebook records for it (filled for every row at
this step, D-2026-10-28-k); any column whose unit says `share` or `rate`
must lie on 0-1. Before the step, `deforestation_forest_rate` and
`informal` were on 0-100 (D-2026-10-06-d, D-2026-10-07-c) while every
other share and rate was on 0-1.

```{r q10-units}
final <- read_rds("_data/final/panel_amz_2000_2020_final.rds")
codebook <- read_csv("_data/aux/codebook.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
ranges <- map_dfr(names(final), function(v) {
  x <- final[[v]]
  tibble(variable = v, class = class(x)[1],
         min = if (is.numeric(x)) min(x, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
         max = if (is.numeric(x)) max(x, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_)
}) %>%
  left_join(codebook %>% select(variable, unit), by = "variable") %>%
  mutate(unit_short = str_replace(unit, " \\(.*$", ""),
         bounded = unit_short %in% c("share", "rate"),
         in_bounds = !bounded | (min >= 0 & max <= 1))
ranges %>% count(unit_short, bounded)
ranges %>% filter(bounded) %>%
  transmute(variable, min = signif(min, 3), max = signif(max, 3), in_bounds)
ranges %>% filter(is.na(unit) | !in_bounds)
```

**Finding.** Every column of the final panel has a codebook unit, and
the 20 columns whose unit is a share or a rate all lie on 0-1:
`deforestation_forest_rate` runs 0 to 0.367 and `informal` 0.286 to
0.984 after the rescale, beside the employment rates and shares, the
crop shares and the two electoral shares that were already on 0-1. No
column is on a percent scale.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-28-h, D-2026-10-28-i (the two rescales at
construction), D-2026-10-28-k (the unit column).
**Assertion.** `04-panel-assemble.R`, output block (`SHARE_RATE_COLS`
on 0-1); `01-env-deforestation.R` and `02-social-census.R`, output
blocks (the rate and the informality share on 0-1).

## Q11. What does the nine-state extension add to the panel, and where are the added municipalities' gaps? (phase 2, step 2.9, 2026-10-29)

What is checked: the 808-municipality panel against the 503 of the biome
sample (task 1.1; D-2026-10-29-a to -d): the two flags; the PPCDAm
municipalities the biome join used to drop (Q2); the source coverage of
the 305 added municipalities block by block; the RAIS municipality-years
missing after installation and the post-2000 municipality-years without
a governing election; the six Mato Grosso municipalities added to the
post-2000 lookup and the parents they add; the pooled z-scores inside
and outside their reference population; and the bonds-per-PIA rates
above one.

```{r q11-flags}
panel %>% filter(year == 2000) %>% count(biome_amazon, legal_amazon)
listed_years <- ppcdam %>%
  filter(ppcdam_list == 1L) %>%
  group_by(geocode) %>%
  summarise(listed = paste(range(year), collapse = "-"), .groups = "drop")
panel %>%
  filter(year == 2000, biome_amazon == 0L, geocode %in% listed_years$geocode) %>%
  select(geocode, municipality, state_abbreviation, legal_amazon) %>%
  left_join(listed_years, by = "geocode")
```

```{r q11-coverage}
added <- panel %>% filter(biome_amazon == 0L)
blocks <- c(ppcdam = "ppcdam_list", bf = "bf_families_n", rais = "emp_workers_n",
            census = "pia", population = "population", gdp = "gdp_brl",
            tse = "elec_enc", area = "munic_area_km2",
            pam = "crop_soy_area_planted_km2", ppm = "cattle_heads",
            prices = "price_index_crop")
yr_range <- function(y) if (length(y) == 0) "" else paste(range(y), collapse = "-")
added %>%
  select(geocode, year, all_of(unname(blocks))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(geocode, year), names_to = "column") %>%
  group_by(column) %>%
  summarise(na_cells = sum(is.na(value)),
            municipalities = n_distinct(geocode[is.na(value)]),
            years = yr_range(year[is.na(value)]), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r q11-gaps}
post2000 <- read_csv("_data/aux/munic_post2000.csv",
                     col_types = cols(.default = col_character(), install_year = col_integer()))
post2000 %>%
  filter(consulted == "2026-10-29") %>%
  select(geocode, municipality, install_year, parent_names, law, law_date)
emp_absent <- added %>%
  filter(is.na(emp_workers_n)) %>%
  left_join(post2000 %>% select(geocode, install_year), by = "geocode") %>%
  mutate(kind = if_else(!is.na(install_year) & year < install_year,
                        "before installation", "gap"))
emp_absent %>% count(kind)
emp_absent %>%
  filter(kind == "gap") %>%
  group_by(municipality, state_abbreviation) %>%
  summarise(years = paste(year, collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(nchar(years)))
added %>%
  filter(year > 2000, is.na(elec_enc)) %>%
  group_by(municipality, state_abbreviation) %>%
  summarise(years = yr_range(year), .groups = "drop")
panel %>%
  filter(year == 2000, muni_parent_split == 1L) %>%
  select(geocode, municipality, state_abbreviation, biome_amazon) %>%
  arrange(geocode)
```

```{r q11-zscores}
panel %>%
  group_by(biome_amazon) %>%
  summarise(across(c(price_index_crop_z, price_index_cattle_z),
                   list(mean = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE), sd = ~ sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE))),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3)))
panel %>%
  filter(emp_pia_rate_total > 1) %>%
  select(municipality, state_abbreviation, year, emp_workers_n, pia, emp_pia_rate_total)
```

**Finding.** The panel has 808 municipalities: 503 in the biome, 269 in
the Legal Amazon outside the biome and 36 outside both (Maranhão's
Cerrado east of the 44th meridian). The four PPCDAm municipalities the
biome join dropped (Q2) are now in the panel, all in the Legal Amazon:
Grajaú (MA, listed 2011-2020) and Comodoro, Paranatinga and Ribeirão
Cascalheira (MT, listed 2023-2024, outside the window). Every source
covers the 305 added municipalities within its window: the gaps are
Bolsa Família before 2004, GDP before 2002, the census-anchored series
before 2010 for the six Mato Grosso municipalities without a 2000
census (60 cells of `pia`), their population in 2000 (6 cells), 35 RAIS
municipality-years (6 before installation, 29 reporting gaps of small
Maranhão and Tocantins municipalities, mostly 2000, plus Serra Nova
Dourada 2001-2002, the only gap after installation in the lookup),
elections for Humberto de Campos 2001-2004, Paranatinga 2009-2012 and
Sambaíba 2017-2020 (no governing election in the file, as for the biome
cases of Q5), and seven crop and six cattle cells before installation.
The six municipalities added to the lookup (D-2026-10-29-b) were created
by Mato Grosso laws of 1998-1999 and installed on 2001-01-01; they bring
the lookup to sixteen rows and the parent flags to seventeen
municipalities, six of them outside the biome; São Félix do Araguaia,
inside the biome, becomes a parent (of Novo Santo Antônio and Serra Nova
Dourada), the one value that moves among the 502 at this step. The
pooled z-scores keep the biome municipality-years as their reference
(D-2026-10-29-c): mean 0 and sd 1 there; outside the biome the crop
z-score has mean 0.96 and sd 2.7, the Cerrado municipalities having
larger crop shares, and the cattle z-score mean -0.07 and sd 0.68. Three cells carry more formal bonds than working-age residents
(Santo Antônio de Leverger, MT, 2000 and 2001; São Salvador do
Tocantins, TO, 2007), so the bonds-per-PIA rates are not bounded by one
and leave the 0-1 guard (D-2026-10-29-d).
**Decision.** D-2026-10-29-a (the sample and the flags), D-2026-10-29-b
(the six lookup municipalities, the RAIS gap after installation),
D-2026-10-29-c (the reference population of the z-scores),
D-2026-10-29-d (the bonds-per-PIA rates above one).
**Assertion.** `04-panel-assemble.R`, raw-state block (808 geocodes with
the two flags, no PPCDAm municipality outside the sample) and output
block (808 × 21 rows; flags constant, biome inside Legal Amazon, 503 and
772; 99 RAIS NA cells; 171 `pia` NA cells; 40 post-2000 election NA
cells; 16 lookup and 17 parent municipalities; the installation rule
with two admitted RAIS gaps; z moments on the reference rows; the five
bonds-per-PIA rates non-negative, three cells above one, the bracket
rates below the total).
